items.stem: Which command substitution captures the output of `date` into the variable `now` in modern Bash?

options.rationale: Correct: $(...) runs the command and assigns its standard output to the variable.
This assigns the literal string 'date', not the command's output.
Angle brackets are used for redirection, not command substitution.
== is a comparison operator; assignment uses a single =.

items.explanation: Correct: $(...) runs the command and assigns its standard output to the variable.

items.stem: A script must stop on the first error and treat unset variables as failures. Which TWO options of `set` help enforce this? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: -e makes the script exit when a command returns a non-zero status.
Correct: -u makes referencing an unset variable an error.
-x prints commands for debugging; it does not change error behaviour.
-v echoes input lines; it does not affect error handling.

items.explanation: Correct: -e exits on error and -u fails on unset variables; together they harden a script.

items.stem: Why can a script that runs fine in an interactive shell fail when run by cron?

options.text: cron runs with a minimal environment and a different PATH
options.rationale: Correct: cron does not load the interactive shell profile, so PATH and variables differ.
cron can run any executable, including Bash scripts.

options.text: cron always runs as a different CPU architecture
options.rationale: cron runs on the same machine and architecture.

options.text: cron strips all comments from the script
options.rationale: cron does not modify the script contents.

items.explanation: Correct: cron uses a minimal environment, so absolute paths and explicit variables are needed.
